```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)

# Import the dataset
nhanes <- read_csv("data/cleaned_NHANES.csv")

# Ensure avg_sbp is calculated if missing
if (!"avg_sbp" %in% colnames(nhanes)) {
  nhanes <- nhanes %>%
    rowwise() %>%
    mutate(
      avg_sbp = if (all(is.na(c_across(starts_with("systolic_bp"))))) NA_real_ else mean(c_across(starts_with("systolic_bp")), na.rm = TRUE)
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```
Introduction
The National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) provides critical data on the health and nutritional status of the population [@nhanes].

Participant Characteristics
The table below outlines the overall sample size, gender distribution, ethnic breakdown, and summary statistics for average systolic blood pressure across each survey wave.
```
# Calculate summary statistics by wave
summary_data <- nhanes %>%
  group_by(wave) %>%
  summarise(
    total_n = n(),
    male_n = sum(gender == "Male", na.rm = TRUE),
    male_pct = round((male_n / total_n) * 100, 1),
    white_n = sum(ethnicity_2 == "White", na.rm = TRUE),
    white_pct = round((white_n / total_n) * 100, 1),
    black_n = sum(ethnicity_2 == "Black", na.rm = TRUE),
    black_pct = round((black_n / total_n) * 100, 1),
    mexican_n = sum(ethnicity_2 == "Mexican", na.rm = TRUE),
    mexican_pct = round((mexican_n / total_n) * 100, 1),
    sbp_min = round(min(avg_sbp, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sbp_max = round(max(avg_sbp, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sbp_median = round(median(avg_sbp, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sbp_mean = round(mean(avg_sbp, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
    sbp_sd = round(sd(avg_sbp, na.rm = TRUE), 1)
  )

# Build the LaTeX-friendly table
summary_data %>%
  kable(
    col.names = c("Wave", "Total N", "N", "%", "White (N)", "White (%)", "Black (N)", "Black (%)", "Mexican (N)", "Mexican (%)", "Min", "Max", "Median", "Mean", "SD"),
    caption = "NHANES Sample Characteristics by Wave",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = "c"
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("scale_down", "hold_position")) %>%
  add_header_above(c(" " = 2, "Males" = 2, "Ethnicity" = 6, "Systolic BP" = 5)) %>%
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE)

```
As demonstrated in the table, the distribution of participants across major demographic categories and the average systolic blood pressure measurements remain relatively consistent across the recorded survey waves.
